This section takes effect in daily work immediately when companion animal travel is handled at the desk.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: to ensure every companion animal is accepted, moved, and documented with steady care, clear direction, and prompt action.

All staff must treat each traveler and pet with calm respect and must give plain, usable guidance without delay. Carriers are to be checked for secure latches, visible identification, and signs of distress before transfer to the ground team. Do not promise any exception unless the required review has been completed and the record is clear. If a condition appears unsafe, stop the handoff at once and escalate through the proper channel.

The desk must keep the path of custody orderly from check-in to aircraft loading and back to release. Speak in short sentences, confirm the travel plan, and make certain the owner understands the next step before the file moves forward. If a companion animal shows agitation, the handler must reduce noise, avoid sudden motion, and protect the animal from unnecessary contact. Use only approved records for notes, and keep the wording factual, brief, and complete.

<<FACT F002>> The desk shall maintain a calm receiving area, and staff must never leave a carrier unattended in a public path. If a transfer is interrupted, the file must reflect the reason and the action taken. <<FACT F019>> Staff must not improvise pet lounge access, and any change to the normal flow requires direct approval through the travel desk lead. All instructions to travelers must remain consistent with safety guidance and the current booking status.

The ground team is responsible for careful movement between services, and the travel desk must support that work with timely confirmation and exact handoff notes. When a traveler such as Samuel Costa, Ethan Ali, or a pet such as Loki is in the system, the record must stay clean, polite, and ready for inspection. Any gap in care, any unclear label, or any mismatch in ownership details must be corrected before release.

Contact the travel desk lead at once for urgent exceptions, welfare concerns, or unresolved documentation.
